w-wisdom.title: The Wisdom of Insecurity
w-wisdom.author: Alan Watts
w-wisdom.reference: 1951; chapters II “Pain and Time”, III “The Great Stream”, V “On Being Aware”, and VI “The Marvelous Moment”. Original paraphrases, no quoted translation.

w-insecurity.title: The Wisdom of Insecurity
w-insecurity.author: Alan Watts
w-insecurity.reference: Chapter V “On Being Aware”: psychological security, the pursuit of safety, and the changing present. Contrast practical necessities with the request for a final inward guarantee.

w-reversed.title: The Wisdom of Insecurity
w-reversed.author: Alan Watts
w-reversed.reference: Preface: reversed effort / the backwards law, breathing and floating illustrations; chapters IV–V on the body and awareness. Sleep illustration here is original.

w-world-self.title: The World As Self, part2
w-world-self.author: Alan Watts
w-world-self.reference: Lecture transcript, 59:42–1:00:43: sleep, digestion, and the paradox of forcing release. Source recording embedded; no reliance on archive summary.

w-present.title: The Wisdom of Insecurity
w-present.author: Alan Watts
w-present.reference: Chapter II “Pain and Time” and VI “The Marvelous Moment”: plans for tomorrow gain significance through present experience.

w-symbols.title: Ecological Awareness
w-symbols.author: Alan Watts
w-symbols.reference: Complete lecture transcript; discussion of abstraction, money, status, symbols, and contact with concrete goods. Source audio is embedded.

w-stream.title: The Wisdom of Insecurity
w-stream.author: Alan Watts
w-stream.reference: Chapter III “The Great Stream”; continuity, flux, symbols, and the mistake of treating living experience as a fixed object.

w-self.title: The Book: On the Taboo Against Knowing Who You Are
w-self.author: Alan Watts
w-self.reference: 1966; chapter 1 “Inside Information” and chapter 3 “How To Be a Genuine Fake”; ego as a conventional picture and the organism as more than that picture.

w-body-world.title: The Book: On the Taboo Against Knowing Who You Are
w-body-world.author: Alan Watts
w-body-world.reference: Chapter4 “The World Is Your Body”; organism/environment polarity and the physical boundary as one part of an interdependent life. Nondual extrapolation is philosophical.

w-ecology.title: Ecological Awareness
w-ecology.author: Alan Watts
w-ecology.reference: Complete lecture transcript: organism and environment as one process viewed from different angles, ecological relationship, narrow symbolic accounts. Source audio embedded.

w-mutual.title: Taoist Way
w-mutual.author: Alan Watts
w-mutual.reference: Part 1, 16:28–21:59: bees and flowers; mutual arising, interdependence, and the polar terms high/low and front/back. Scientific generalizations treated carefully.

w-opposites.title: The Book: On the Taboo Against Knowing Who You Are
w-opposites.author: Alan Watts
w-opposites.reference: Chapter2 “The Game of Black-and-White”: polar relationships, figure/ground, and the attempted elimination of a contrasting pole.

w-breath.title: Meditation
w-breath.author: Alan Watts
w-breath.reference: Essential Lectures, Program 3 (1972), 15:06–17:08: breathing viewed as voluntary and involuntary activity. Primary recording transcript; no breath-exercise prescription.

w-individual.title: Individual and the World
w-individual.author: Alan Watts
w-individual.reference: Complete lecture transcript; the body/mind beyond the narrow “I”, voluntary and involuntary activity, and relation to the environment.

w-controller.title: Individual and the World
w-controller.author: Alan Watts
w-controller.reference: Complete lecture transcript; thinker separated from thoughts, feeling-controller divided from feelings, and the desire to control everything.

w-double-bind.title: The Book: On the Taboo Against Knowing Who You Are
w-double-bind.author: Alan Watts
w-double-bind.reference: Chapter3 “How To Be a Genuine Fake”; social demand to become a free agent through obedience, ego training and the double bind.

w-work.title: Work and Play
w-work.author: Alan Watts
w-work.reference: Essential Lectures, Program 7 (1972), 02:09–05:01 and 22:33–25:18: work/play distinction, artistic practice, and pleasure in listening to a note. Primary recording transcript.

w-play.title: Play and Survival
w-play.author: Alan Watts
w-play.reference: Complete primary lecture transcript; activity as means versus the value of play and the doing itself.

w-music.title: Meditation
w-music.author: Alan Watts
w-music.reference: Essential Lectures, Program 3 (1972), 04:59–06:11: music, dance, and the mistake of treating the last chord as the purpose of a piece. Primary recording transcript.

w-tao.title: Taoist Way
w-tao.author: Alan Watts
w-tao.reference: Part 2, 24:04ff: wu wei as “not forcing”, key/lock and wood-grain examples; broader discussion of the course of nature. Original illustrative language.

w-watercourse.title: Tao: The Watercourse Way
w-watercourse.author: Alan Watts
w-watercourse.reference: Posthumous 1975 book completed with Al Chung-liang Huang; chapter III “Tao”, pp. 48–50, and IV “Wu-wei”, pp. 75–77. Water, yielding, and action responsive to existing patterns. Public scan verified by direct download.

w-impermanence.title: The Wisdom of Insecurity
w-impermanence.author: Alan Watts
w-impermanence.reference: ChaptersIII “The Great Stream” and VI “The Marvelous Moment”; experience as movement, insecurity, and the impossibility of fixing living change.

w-faith.title: Relevance of Oriental Philosophy
w-faith.author: Alan Watts
w-faith.reference: Primary lecture transcript; faith as openness versus clinging to ideas and opinions. Distinction uses Watts’s chosen terminology.

w-religion.title: The Wisdom of Insecurity
w-religion.author: Alan Watts
w-religion.reference: ChapterI “The Age of Anxiety” and IX “Religion Reviewed”; faith, belief, insecurity and openness to reality.

w-sincerity.title: Play and Sincerity
w-sincerity.author: Alan Watts
w-sincerity.reference: Complete primary lecture transcript; play/seriousness, sincere participation, and the performance of a divided self. Source audio embedded.

w-spotlight.title: Transformation of Consciousness
w-spotlight.author: Alan Watts
w-spotlight.reference: Part 2 “Seeing Past Words”; around 1:55:29 spotlight of conscious attention versus wider floodlight awareness. Metaphor treated as philosophical, not an established attention model.

w-social-self.title: Individual and the World
w-social-self.author: Alan Watts
w-social-self.reference: Complete primary lecture transcript; social conventions, the narrow meaning of “I”, personality and the organism beyond a conventional identity.
